newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up 30 bps to 11.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up 30 bps to 11.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate rose 30 basis points to 11.8 percent on Monday as some borrowers offered funds at higher rates, dealers said.
They put the daily trade at 34 million kuna, leaving 29 million kuna surplus on the suply side. Demand for another 500,000 kuna was not met as borrowers and lenders failed to agree on terms.
Fresh borrowing accounted for 29.2 million kuna, mostly call money loans at a rate of 11 percent.
Term loans were granted at rates varying from 11 percent to 16 percent for two smaller short-term loans.
Insurers rolled over previous 1.8 million kuna loans at 15 percent, up from Friday's 10-14 percent range.
The central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Tuesday slightly weaker at 5.7959 against the dollar and 3.5632 against the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
